itemUsage.en: Supporter Operator Astgenne, on a brand-new journey of exploration again.
itemUsage.zh: 辅助干员星源，在探索的道路上又一次开始了全新的旅程。

itemDesc.en: A scientist's future ought to be bound by neither limits nor fear, and she has never forgotten her own path.
itemDesc.zh: 科学家的明天应当是无限而又无所畏惧的，她从未忘记自己的前路。

description.en: The next attack targets the furthest <@ba.vup>{max_target_attack}</> enemies from the Objective Point within Attack Range, dealing <@ba.vup>{atk_scale:0%}</> ATK as Arts damage; extends <$ba.sluggish>Slow</> duration to <@ba.vup>{sluggish}</> seconds, links to up to <@ba.vup>{max_target}</> enemies around the target and pulls them towards the target's location with <@ba.vup>slight</> force, dealing the same amount of Arts damage

description.en: Attack range <@ba.vup>expands</>; <@ba.vup>+{atk:0%}</> ATK, ATK interval <@ba.vup>decreases</>; attacks continuously lock onto <@ba.vup>{attack@max_target}</> enemies, chaining them together, and every chained enemy will deal <@ba.vup>{attack@atk_share:0%}</> of the Arts damage taken to other chained enemies as extra damage
description.zh: 攻击范围<@ba.vup>扩大</>，攻击力<@ba.vup>+{atk:0%}</>，攻击间隔<@ba.vup>缩短</>，持续锁定<@ba.vup>{attack@max_target}</>个敌人进行攻击，被锁定的敌人会互相链接；每个被链接的敌人会把即将受到法术伤害的<@ba.vup>{attack@atk_share:0%}</>额外传导给其他链接目标

Operator Astgenne the Lightchaser has demonstrated a remarkable aptitude for impeding the enemy.

description.en: The end of an adventure does not mean the end of paperwork. In fact, it usually means the start of it. Astgenne piles her travel notes and survey records on one side of her desk. As she begins to write up a self-reflection report on how she left her post without leave, Muelsyse drops by with some news for her. 'Elena, some kiddos at the observation station door say they've got stuff for you.' 'Got it, be right there.' Villagers visiting was hardly anything new. After Rhine Lab arrived in Kjerag, the first thing they did was send out several teams of field investigators to perform geographical surveys. The nearby villages were natural first contacts, and from this back-and-forth, a vague sense of friendship and camaraderie began to form behind the curiosity. However, it proved far too frail in the face of Catastrophe. Enmity, panic, and ideas from both within and without Kjerag spread like wildfire. In the face of all this, that vague friendship changed, going through many ups and downs before finally, once the dust had settled, turning into remorse. 'Sorry, Miss...' The leader of the children presses a box she had been cradling into her hands, avoiding her gaze. It is a finely-carved wooden box, made with great care by a local craftsman. Within are several small square compartments, each crammed with ore pieces in many different sizes, covered with marks from rough polishing. 'Did you find these minerals yourself?' '...Yeah, we did.' The leader scratches her head, a little unnaturally. 'We wanted to give you something to apologize, but we didn't know what to get you, because it's like... you already have everything you need here.' 'It was our village's new teacher who taught us what to do!' Another girl, even younger than the first, can't hold herself back. 'He said, we should give you something you want then, or something you like!' Astgenne lowers her head, not quite sure whether to laugh or cry. These children had only just started their schooling, and their innocent minds had led them to believe that the researchers scouring the snow and streams were looking for ore. After all, as far as they were concerned, there was nothing else up in the mountains. 'Did we... pick the wrong thing?' One child asks quietly. 'Can't be...' The girl who piped up wrinkles her brow in worry. 'Didn't the adults say they came to Kjerag to look at the stars? The stones on the ground are pretty much the same as the stars in the sky, aren't they?' 'Would you mind telling me more about them?' Astgenne, who had stayed silent the whole time, walks into the middle of the group. She cradles the box, carefully brushing the snow off its lid. 'Since we're such good friends now, I'd like to hear the stories you know. Stories about the stones on the ground, and the stars in the sky.'
description.zh:
冒险的结束从不是文书工作的结束，不如说，那正是它们的开端。
星源把自己一路的笔记与探测记录堆叠在桌子一侧，新建出一份名叫擅自离岗检讨的文档的时候，缪尔赛思为她带来了一个新的消息。
“埃琳娜，有几个孩子在观测站门口，说有东西要交给你。”
“知道了，我这就去。”
有村民来访并不是新奇消息。莱茵抵达谢拉格后，立刻派出了几支由调查员组成的队伍负责地理勘测。周边村落自然是第一接触目标，如此你来我往的接触之中，模糊的友情与好意在好奇之中初见雏形，只是一切还太脆弱，未能巩固就遇上了天灾。
对抗，恐慌，属于与不属于谢拉格人的想法开始在民间散播，模糊的好意在仓皇中急转直下，经历几番跌宕起伏，最终在万事分明的当下生成一片愧疚之意。
“抱歉，姐姐……”为首的孩子将怀中的盒子塞给她，似乎不敢看她的眼睛。
那是一个精巧的木匣子，是本地匠人花了心思做的，内里分出数个小方格形的空间，分别填满了不同的矿石切块，大小不一，遍布粗糙的手工打磨痕迹。
“这些矿物是你们亲自去找的吗？”
“……是，是我们找的。”带头的孩子有些不自然地挠头，“我们本来想给你赔礼道歉，却不知道能送什么，因为你们这儿好像……好像什么都不缺。”
“是村里新来的老师教我们的！”另一个年纪更小的女孩忍不住抢答道，“他说，应该送你需要、你喜欢的东西！”
星源哭笑不得地低下头。
这些孩子才刚开始接受教育，他们简单地认为，在雪堆与山涧中翻翻找找的调查员所需要的是矿石——毕竟对于他们来说，山上并没有除此之外的任何东西了。
“我们……送错了吗？”一个孩子小声地问。
“不至于吧……”那个抢答的孩子担忧地皱着脸，“那些大人不都说，这些哥哥姐姐们来谢拉格是为了看星星吗？地上的石头，本就是天空中的星星呀，它们不是一样的吗？”
“能多和我讲讲吗？”原本沉默的星源走入他们之间，她抱着那个木盒，用心地拂去落在顶上的雪，“既然我们已经是好朋友了，我也想听你们知道的故事。关于地上的石头，与空中的星星的故事。”
